record.paper_title: OPEN QUESTIONS FOR OPERATORS RELATED TO RECTANGULAR CATALAN COMBINATORICS
record.context_brief: e-positive refinements of Schur inclusions at t = 1 + r
record.original_question: For integers m,n ≥ 1, let e_{m,n}(x;q,1+r) and h_{m,n}(x;q,1+r) denote the t = 1 + r specializations of the symmetric functions attached to the elementary and complete homogeneous seeds, with d = gcd(m,n), α the exponent from the inclusion q^α e_{m-1,n} into e_{m,n}, and β = α(m,n) - d + 1 the exponent from the inclusion into (-qt)^(1-d) h_{m,n}. In the e-positivity order ≤_e, can one prove q^α e_{m-1,n}(x;q,1+r) ≤_e e_{m,n}(x;q,1+r) and q^β e_{m-1,n}(x;q,1+r) ≤_e (-qt)^(1-d) h_{m,n}(x;q,1+r) for all m,n ≥ 1, and give a combinatorial explanation of these inequalities?

evidence.quote: Question.9. Can we prove that qα em−1,n(x; q, 1 + r) ≤e em,n(x; q, 1 + r), and qβ em−1,n(x; q, 1 + r) ≤e (−qt)1−dhm,n(x; q, 1 + r). for all m, n ≥ 1, and explain this combinatorially?
qβ em−1,n(x; q, t) ⪯s (−qt)1−dhm,n(x; q, t), with β = α(m, n) − d + 1, for d = gcd(m, n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the ring $\Lambda(x)[q,t]$ of symmetric functions in variables $x = (x_1, x_2, \dots)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$. Let $\{e_\lambda\}$ denote the elementary basis of $\Lambda$. For two symmetric-function-valued polynomials $A, B$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}[q,t]$, write $A \le_e B$ (the e-positivity order) if $B - A$ expands in the basis $\{e_\lambda\}$ with coefficients lying in $\mathbb{N}[q,t]$.

For positive integers $m, n \ge 1$, let $e_{m,n}(x;q,t)$ and $h_{m,n}(x;q,t)$ denote the symmetric functions associated to the elementary and complete-homogeneous "rectangular" seeds in the rectangular Catalan setting, and set $d = \gcd(m,n)$. Suppose there exist nonnegative integer exponents $\alpha = \alpha(m,n)$ and $\beta = \alpha(m,n) - d + 1$ such that, in the analogous Schur-positivity order $\preceq_s$,
$$q^{\alpha} e_{m-1,n}(x;q,t) \preceq_s e_{m,n}(x;q,t), \qquad q^{\beta} e_{m-1,n}(x;q,t) \preceq_s (-qt)^{1-d}\, h_{m,n}(x;q,t).$$

Now specialize $t = 1+r$ where $r$ is a formal parameter, and write $f(x;q,1+r)$ for this specialization. Prove or disprove that for all integers $m, n \ge 1$,
$$q^{\alpha}\, e_{m-1,n}(x;q,1+r) \;\le_e\; e_{m,n}(x;q,1+r),$$
$$q^{\beta}\, e_{m-1,n}(x;q,1+r) \;\le_e\; (-q(1+r))^{1-d}\, h_{m,n}(x;q,1+r),$$
and provide a combinatorial interpretation of the resulting nonnegative coefficients.

artifact.status_search_result: No direct evidence was found resolving these specific e-positivity inequalities at the t = 1+r specialization for the rectangular Catalan operators. Related literature on (q,t)-Catalan positivity exists, but a proof or refutation of these particular refined e-positivity statements with combinatorial explanation could not be confirmed.

status_evidence.title: (q,t)-Catalan polynomials – François Bergeron
status_evidence.snippet: Resource page on (q,t)-Catalan polynomials and rectangular Catalan combinatorics; lists open questions but no specific resolution of these e-positivity inequalities at t=1+r.
status_evidence.claim: No reported resolution of the specific e-positivity refinements at t = 1+r.

status_evidence.title: A Proof of the q,t-Catalan Positivity Conjecture (Haglund)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes positivity for the q,t-Catalan numbers but does not address the specific e-positivity inclusions for q^alpha e_{m-1,n} into e_{m,n} or h_{m,n} at t=1+r.
status_evidence.claim: Existing positivity results do not cover the stated refinements.
